SEP 28 UPDATE - THE 'DIVERSITY' GATE WAS A DEFECT, NOW FIXED. Baseline regenerated deliberately.
assembler.js multiplied a candidate by diversityPenalty (0.6) when its primary entity was already covered twice, THEN compared it to minScore (0.12). In a self-scoped world nearly every fact has entity:you as primary, so after two picks every remaining fact (0.173 -> 0.104) fell under the floor together and was dropped with reason 'diversity' (q001: 12 candidates in, 3 out, 194 of 1600 chars used). Diversity was documented as a RE-RANKING and implemented as a GATE. Fix: minScore judges worth BEFORE crowding; diversity only reorders. Pinned in src/brain/tests/contextSelfCrowding.test.js (2 of 4 tests fail against the old assembler).
MOVEMENT (context-core): recall_at_8 0.6786 -> 0.7560 | mrr 0.6448 -> 0.6696 | ndcg_at_8 0.6151 -> 0.6542 | recall_superseded 0.30 -> 0.60 | recall_temporal 0.56 -> 0.68 | recall_negation 0.70 -> 0.80 | recall_direct 0.9636 -> 1.0 | recall_category 0.375 -> 0.469 | recall_selfword 0.625 -> 0.75. noise_lines 13 -> 18 (REGRESSED, accepted: the extra lines are the floor's own inherited noise, which the CE was hiding by dropping answers with it; the floor emits 16).
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the CE now EQUALS the floor's recall (0.7560) - it does not beat it - and is still slightly behind on mrr (-0.017), ndcg (-0.017), top1_kind (-0.042) with 2 more noise lines. This lands exactly on the ceiling the paragraph below already recorded ('best available CE reaches EXACTLY the floor's recall'). The conclusion below STANDS: value must come from something the floor lacks (dense lane: retrieval-dense/world-model-lift show recall 0.845). Whether to keep AQUA_CONTEXT_V2=on in production is an open owner decision; this fix makes 'on' no longer lose answers, it does not make 'on' better than 'off'.
--- ORIGINAL NOTE (Aug 30) FOLLOWS ---
FIRST measurement of the path production actually reads. routes/chat.js:587 sends the turn through Brain.assembleContext with PIC as the FLOOR, and AQUA_CONTEXT_V2=on ships in the environment template — so retrieval-core.v1 has been grading an intermediate stage the Context Engine overrides before anything reaches the model.

THE CONTEXT ENGINE IS CURRENTLY WORSE THAN THE FLOOR IT WRAPS. Same world, same 200 queries, same shared scorer (retrievalScoring.mjs); the only variable is which function is asked:
  recall_at_8        0.7560 -> 0.6786   (-0.077)
  mrr                0.6865 -> 0.6448
  ndcg_at_8          0.6710 -> 0.6151
  top1_kind          0.5714 -> 0.5298
  recall_direct      1.0000 -> 0.9636   (it loses answers on the EASIEST category)
  recall_superseded  0.6000 -> 0.3000   (halved)
  recall_temporal    0.6800 -> 0.5600
  recall_negation    0.8000 -> 0.7000
It buys 3 fewer noise lines (16 -> 13) at that price. unknown_honesty is unchanged.

CAUSE, TRACED: the assembler rescores the floor's pool on ten dimensions, and the floor's own relevance score — the factAffinity number that knows what the question ASKED — is not one of them and is not passed in. gatherCandidates drops it, along with entityIds and timestamp. So the layer that decides what reaches the model ranks on ten importance signals and zero relevance signals. That is the same defect the PIC gate was built to close one layer down ('an expression in which the QUESTION does not appear'), reproduced above it.

13 of 168 answerable queries lose their answer entirely to this.

═══ THE QUESTION IS NOW CLOSED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO ═══

Four configurations were built and measured across sessions:
  as-shipped                              recall 0.6786   noise 13
  relevance carried as an 11th dimension  recall 0.7321   noise 14
  the same, normalised per query          recall 0.7560   noise 18
  floor exempt from BOTH minScore gates   recall 0.7560   noise 17
  ── the floor itself ──                  recall 0.7560   noise 16

The best available Context Engine reaches EXACTLY the floor's recall and one
noise line worse. It is therefore strictly worse than switching it off: same
recall, more noise, and a layer of code on the turn path.

THE OBVIOUS REMAINING FIX WAS MEASURED BEFORE BEING BUILT, AND THE SIGNAL IS
NOT THERE. Having the CE abstain when nothing in the pool is relevant enough
requires the two populations to separate on the floor's score. They do not —
top relevance per query over the same 200:
  answerable      p10 0.000   p25 0.333   median 0.575
  noisy silence   min 0.250   median 0.500   max 0.600
The noisy population sits INSIDE the answerable one:
  T=0.30  removes 1 of 16 noise lines,  silences 32 of 168 answerable queries
  T=0.35  removes 3 of 16,              silences 43 of 168
  T=0.45  removes 8 of 16,              silences 55 of 168

AND THE NOISE WAS NEVER THE CE'S TO FIX. Traced per query: the floor emits 16
lines across 9 silence queries and NEVER abstains on any of them; the CE
inherits 12 and adds 1 from its own reach lane. It is inherited, not generated.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE DECISION. The CE's value cannot come from re-ranking
what the floor hands it — the floor's score is the only relevance signal it
has, and that score does not separate 'I found the answer' from 'I found
something person-shaped'. Value has to come from something the floor does NOT
have: embeddings, typed claims, project or file context. Until one of those
lands, AQUA_CONTEXT_V2=off measures better than any version of it that exists.
Pinned in eval/tests/contextBaseline.test.js.

Regenerate with: npm run eval:gate -- context-core --update
